pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: clients/typescript/src/http.ts:79 The one transport door asserts that a parsed body is the caller's `T`. There is no named marker and no written invariant at the cast (the same holds at http.ts:105 and :110 for ndjson lines), so the type guarantee every SDK caller relies on is asserted, not checked, and cannot be audited by grep.

techniques.evidence: clients/typescript/src/http.ts:79 The region is enclosed: all reads go through getJson/streamNdjson. It is not marked, and it carries no invariant stating why the body is a T (for example, 'the server emits the generated schema'). A bare `as T` is indistinguishable from an ordinary cast.

clients/typescript/src/sync.ts:101 The per-page apply/stall/dedupe decision is a pure function from revisions to a plan. The async PumperSync loop is the driver, and the tests call planPage directly with no fetch double.

clients/typescript/src/http.ts:6 The network is the seam. Tests substitute fetch through the config (conformance.test.ts fakeFetch/fetchSpy), and all reads pass through http.ts. sinkFor (sync.ts:158) is a single substitution point for dry runs.

clients/typescript/src/types.ts:61 The SDK narrows the generated open `change: string` to a closed union, so consumers can switch exhaustively. That moves the accepted-value set into the checked half of the interface.
clients/typescript/src/sync.ts:361 Callers learn two verbs and get snapshot vs. incremental, paging, checkpointing and tombstoning. The PumperSync class stays private, which is high leverage.

clients/typescript/src/sync.ts:118 One pass builds the latest-per-key map and the skip counters together, with an early stall return. That is the multiple-outputs case, where an explicit loop is the right form.
clients/typescript/src/sync.ts:301 The async driver calls a synchronous core. The flow-control model (await) stays in the loop and never enters the decision logic.
